children: Shares of Finnish nuclear technology company Steady Energy (STEADY.HE) fell nearly 6% on their market debut on Nasdaq Helsinki First North on Friday, after opening in line with the €10.00 per share price in its oversubscribed initial public offering (IPO).

The listing comes amid growing interest in nuclear energy as Europe prepares for higher power demand from cloud computing and data-centre expansion, while municipalities seek low-carbon alternatives to fossil-fuel heating.
Steady Energy develops small modular reactor (SMR) technology aimed at replacing combustion-based heating sources.
Its LDR-50 nuclear heating reactors are targeted for installation in municipalities with more than 50,000 citizens.
Four Finnish cities are exploringthe use of Steady Energy's LDR-50 reactors for district heating.
The group was founded in 2023 as a spin-off from VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland.
The IPO, aimed at raising gross proceeds of €5 million ($5.63 million), was oversubscribed, prompting an early closure of the subscription period.
